title: Align billing export hour boundaries and coupon/credit offsets to prevent invoice drift
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers reported invoice delta between Stripe charges and NetSuite invoice lines for mid-cycle adjustments (coupons/credits and burst quota refunds). Root cause appears to be twofold: (1) our hourly usage rollup job currently uses local-hour bucket boundaries which drift during DST transitions and when UTC vs account timezone conversions are applied, causing split token/embedding usage to be assigned to adjacent invoice periods; (2) the credit/coupon application pipeline applies offsets after export grouping which yields negative line allocations that do not consistently map to NetSuite line allocation logic, producing duplicate or missing prorated invoice rows.

Impact: Incorrect invoice amounts for a subset (~0.6%) of customers with mid-cycle subscription changes, coupons, or burst credits. This leads to customer disputes, manual adjustments by finance, and exposure in revenue recognition.

Scope: Fix the export alignment and produce a one-off correction job to regenerate invoice allocations for impacted accounts. Work touches the hourly-usage-rollup service, the stripe-exporter reconciliation layer, and NetSuite line mapper. Also update unit/integration tests and dashboards to detect regressions.
investigation_findings: Found ~1,182 export rows in last 90 days where usage bucket timestamp was within 60s of hour boundary; 73% of these correlate with accounts that changed billing timezone or had DST during the interval.

SQL query (simplified) used to identify anomalies: SELECT account_id, date_trunc('hour', timestamp AT TIME ZONE account_tz) as bucket, sum(units) FROM usage_events WHERE timestamp BETWEEN X AND Y GROUP BY 1,2 HAVING count(*) > 1;
Stripe export writes idempotency_token but NetSuite mapping used aggregation by (account, date, sku) causing duplicate allocations when coupon offsets were negative.
Edge-case: when a coupon fully offsets a prorated subscription line, we were creating a zero-value line in NetSuite rather than collapsing it, which caused rounding differences across exports.

Temporary mitigations applied: changed exporter to align to UTC hour boundaries for new exports and added a guard that prevents creating zero-value invoice lines in NetSuite mapping (hotfix deployed 2026-03-09).
proposed_solution: 1) Normalize export bucket boundaries to UTC internally and perform account timezone presentation only in the Console UI. This avoids DST and conversion drift for accounting pipelines. 2) Update the coupon/credit allocation logic to: - apply credits at the same stage as aggregation (before grouping/line creation), - ensure negative offsets are represented as adjustment lines with explicit reference ids and idempotency tokens that map to Stripe ledger entries, - collapse zero-value lines. 3) Add deterministic idempotency keys (account+period+adjustment_type+hash) to all export rows so replays are safe. 4) Implement a one-off correction pipeline to recompute and re-export affected invoice allocations for the last 120 days; write a NetSuite-safe delta file format and a reconcile report for Finance. 5) Add monitoring: anomalies-percentage, bucket-boundary-variance, and daily reconciliation job alerts.
acceptance_criteria: New exports use UTC-aligned buckets; verified by sampling exports for 7 days and confirming no bucket time drift across DST events.
Coupon/credit offsets are applied pre-aggregation and produce the same line counts and totals when replayed across environments (staging vs prod).
Re-run of correction job for a sampled list of impacted accounts reconciles Stripe charges and NetSuite invoice lines within accepted rounding tolerance (< $0.50 per invoice).
Finance has received the delta report and accepted the correction format and has an approved manual fallback for any remaining disputes.
New unit/integration tests cover idempotency key collisions and zero-value line collapse.
task_breakdown: ENG: Update usage rollup service to emit UTC bucket timestamps and add conversion tests (3 pts).
ENG: Refactor stripe-exporter to apply coupon offsets before grouping and attach deterministic idempotency keys (2 pts).
ENG/FIN: Design NetSuite delta file format and run validation with sandbox (2 pts).
ENG: Implement correction pipeline and dry-run mode (3 pts).
QA: Add end-to-end replay tests and integrate with CI (2 pts).
Observability: Add dashboards and alerts for bucket-boundary anomalies (1 pt).
Docs: Update billing runbook with steps for re-export and dispute handling (1 pt).
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy UTC-bucket change to a single ingestion region and run export dry-runs for one week against staging NetSuite. Phase 2: enable coupon pre-aggregation in stripe-exporter behind a feature flag and re-run validation. Phase 3: run correction pipeline in dry-run for last 120 days, produce delta files for Finance, and after sign-off, publish NetSuite delta imports. Phase 4: monitor metrics for 7 days and disable feature flag fallback. Backout plan: revert exports to local-hour mode and restore previous exporter state; idempotency keys ensure safe replay and avoid duplication.
data_migration_and_fix_plan: - Identify impacted accounts via anomaly query and store list in billing-corrections S3 prefix. - Correction pipeline recomputes aggregation and produces a delta CSV with: account_id, period_utc_hour, original_line_id, corrected_amount_cents, reason_code, idempotency_key. - Run reconciliation in NetSuite sandbox; Finance reviews. - Apply to production with low-traffic windows and tracking runbook steps. - Post-apply, run revenue-recognition validation against GL accounts. Expected runtime: ~4 hours for 120 days window for 5k accounts on current infra.
testing_plan: Unit tests for time bucketing and idempotency. Integration tests replaying historical usage through the exporter and validating aggregated totals equal Stripe ledger exports. QA will run a set of 150 synthetic accounts across timezone boundaries (including DST) in staging. We'll also add an assertion: daily export row count per account should not change by >1% after change unless due to valid re-aggregation (tracked in PR description).
monitoring_and_alerting: alert: correction-pipeline-failures -> Slack #billing-ops and email finance@redwood.com
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Correction pipeline may produce additional differences if rounding rules between Stripe and NetSuite differ. Mitigation: include revenue-ops in validation and add rounding-normalization layer that mirrors NetSuite rounding rules.
Risk: Large re-export could impact export throughput during correction. Mitigation: throttle correction jobs and run during off-peak windows; instrumentation to abort if queue grows beyond threshold.
Risk: Unexpected idempotency collisions. Mitigation: deterministic key design review and 2-week shadow mode where both old and new keys are emitted for monitoring.
